name: Buddhism
hook: Four Noble Truths, nirvana and the sound of one hand: Buddhism's recurring six.

facts.label: the Four Noble Truths
facts.statement: The Four Noble Truths begin with the truth that existence is suffering (dukkha) and end with the cessation of suffering.

facts.label: nirvana
facts.statement: Nirvana is Buddhism's state of absolute blessedness, from Sanskrit for "to blow out"; it is the goal of the path.

facts.label: Zen
facts.statement: Zen's two main Japanese schools are Soto and Rinzai, started by Dogen and Eisai in the 12th century; its koans ask about the sound of one hand.

facts.label: the Dalai Lama
facts.statement: The Dalai Lama heads Tibetan Buddhism's Yellow Hat (Gelug) sect; the title goes back more than 600 years, and lama means "superior one."

facts.label: India
facts.statement: Buddhism began in India but had largely died out there by the 12th century, though India is credited with giving it to Asia.

facts.label: the Abhidharma Pitaka
facts.statement: Buddhism's scriptures are divided into "baskets"; the Abhidharma Pitaka is one of those baskets, or texts.

facts.label: Kukai
facts.statement: Kukai, also called Kobo Daishi, brought esoteric Shingon Buddhism to Japan.
